purpose: Painterly reference boards and material atlas for six 8x8 strategic-site models

referencePrompts.radio:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: characterful environment modeling reference for Animal Factory, a painterly isometric tactical game.
Create a clean landscape concept sheet for ONE RADIO TOWER SITE, with an intact version on the left and the same site destroyed on the right. Each site occupies the same complete 8 by 8 square game-tile pad, viewed from the same three-quarter elevated isometric angle. Entire towers visible, no cropped tips. A subtle 8x8 ground grid is visible.
Intact: a tapered four-legged open steel lattice radio mast, about nine tiles tall, with bold alternating weathered rust-red and warm ivory bands, antenna whips, two small microwave dishes, planted on four concrete footings. A small olive-green service hut with vented panels occupies one corner, a coiled maintenance cable and utility cabinet near it. Very readable open lattice silhouette. All stays within the 8x8 pad.
Destroyed: same concrete footings and service hut positions, mast folded and crumpled in two substantial sections across its own pad, bent girders, snapped aerials and scorched battered hut. Recognizable red/ivory fragments. Stable ground-supported wreckage; no floating debris, no giant crater, no active explosion or smoke. Keep every fragment within the 8x8 footprint.
Style: hand-painted game illustration, confident textured brush planes, bright warm edge highlights, rich ochre rust, cream concrete, olive paint and deep charcoal recesses. Sculptural structure with painted material detail, not photoreal, not plastic toy. Neutral grey background around the two ground pads. No characters, no text, no labels or dimensions.
referencePrompts.radar:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: environment modeling reference for Animal Factory, a painterly isometric tactical game.
Create a clean landscape concept sheet for ONE RADAR TOWER SITE, intact on the left and the same site destroyed on the right, same three-quarter elevated isometric camera. Each site fits wholly on an 8 by 8 square game-tile pad with a subtle 8x8 ground grid.
Intact: a broad shallow concave olive-green radar dish with visible pale segmented metal panels, ribs and a prominent central feed strut, mounted in a rust-red swivel yoke on a stout four-legged steel trestle tower. Total height about six game tiles, dish about four tiles across, clearly different from a radio mast. A low olive service control hut stands at the rear corner; four concrete foundation pads and cables. A small grated maintenance deck beneath the swivel. All parts remain inside the footprint.
Destroyed: same site layout, buckled trestle leaning down, dish lying against the collapsed steel support with one broad sector broken off and bent panel edges, central feed snapped, dark scorches, exposed rusty ribs; scorched control hut in its original corner. Ground-supported debris within the same 8x8 footprint. No fireball, no smoke, no flying pieces.
Style: richly hand-painted tactical game art; textured brush facets, warm ivory concrete, olive enamel, rust-red steel, warm bright edges and dark graphic recesses. Clear broad silhouette; detail belongs in paint, not countless fiddly parts. Neutral grey background around the pads. No characters, no words, no labels.
referencePrompts.sam:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: environment modeling reference for Animal Factory, a painterly isometric tactical game.
Create a clean landscape concept sheet for ONE FICTIONAL SAM SITE, intact at left and its destroyed form at right. Both viewed at the same elevated three-quarter isometric angle, both wholly contained on the same 8 by 8 square game-tile hardstanding with a subtle 8x8 grid.
Intact: a fixed olive-green surface-to-air missile emplacement, not a vehicle: a broad circular turntable firmly mounted to a low reinforced concrete foundation, two substantial parallel launch rails angled upward with TWO slim ivory missiles with red nose caps and simple cruciform tail fins. Clear visible trunnion mount and sturdy bracing. A small olive control cabinet and cables behind the launcher. Mid-century fictional military-industrial visual language matching a farm-worker tactical game; no technical schematics. Launcher roughly three tiles high, never a towering rocket or four launch tubes.
Destroyed: same foundation and cabinet positions, a visibly collapsed bent twin-rail assembly with one snapped and blackened missile fuselage lying on the pad, one empty torn rail, scorched olive panels and a dented disconnected nose cone. Low, recognizable mechanical wreckage supported by the base/ground, all inside the 8x8 area. No active explosion, no smoke, no people.
Painterly skin style: bold textured brush planes, warm cream highlights, rust-red exposed metal, olive chipped enamel, deep charcoal joints. Clear silhouettes and painted small detail. Not photoreal or plastic. Neutral grey backdrop around the pads. No text, no logos or labels.

atlasPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Rework the painted materials of these three reference images into a SINGLE practical 3D GAME TEXTURE ATLAS, a rectangular sheet with EXACTLY FOUR columns and TWO rows, eight equal square material swatches. References 1-3 are style/color sources only, do NOT reproduce buildings, missiles or structures.
Top row left to right: 1 muted vermilion/rust-red painted metal with restrained ochre chips, 2 warm ivory painted metal with subtle dirty streaks and brushed cream highlights, 3 aged olive-green enamel with painted lighter brush facets and sparse exposed rust flecks, 4 pale warm grey concrete with subtle worn cracks and mineral brush texture.
Bottom row left to right: 5 charcoal blue-grey raw steel with steel-grey painterly highlights, 6 charred blackened steel with ash-grey patches and a few rusty scorched edges, 7 burnt sienna oxidized steel with layered orange-rust brush planes, 8 soot-stained dark grey concrete and ash.
Every square is a flat evenly lit orthographic seamless material field filling its entire cell. No perspective, no dramatic light, no bevel, no outer edge, no inset borders or gutters, no labels or objects. Use small subdued variation within broad painterly planes, avoid harsh repeating stripes or shiny noise. High contrast comes from the modeled edges, not a glowing texture. Match the confident illustrated brushwork of the reference boards. This atlas will be sampled onto simple real 3D geometry. Opaque background. Wide 2:1 sheet, four equal columns and two equal rows with precisely aligned boundaries.
